artists.biography:
Tori Amos (born Myra Ellen Amos; August 22, 1963) is an American pianist, singer-songwriter and composer. She is a classically trained musician and possesses a mezzo-soprano vocal range. Amos originally served as the lead singer of 1980s synthpop group Y Kant Tori Read, and as a solo artist was at the forefront of a number of female singer-songwriters in the early 1990s. She was also noteworthy early in her solo career as one of the few alternative rock performers to use a piano as her primary instrument. Some of her charting singles include "Crucify", "Silent All These Years", "God", "Cornflake Girl", "Caught a Lite Sneeze", "Professional Widow", "Spark", "1000 Oceans", and "A Sorta Fairytale", her most commercially successful single in the U.S. to date.
 
As of 2005, Amos had sold 12 million albums worldwide. She has been nominated for several awards, including 8 Grammy Award nominations. Amos was also named one of People Magazine's 50 Most Beautiful People in 1996.

perplexity.description:
Released in January 1994 on Atlantic Records, Under the Pink is the second studio album by American singer-songwriter Tori Amos. Musically, the album blends alternative rock with piano-driven art pop, marked by Amos’s distinctive use of complex chord structures, occasional dissonance, and emotionally charged vocals. The record showcases a dynamic sonic range, moving from delicate keyboard explorations to brash, experimental rock, with lyrics that delve into themes of femininity, identity, and personal trauma. Its sound has been compared to artists like Joni Mitchell and Kate Bush, reflecting Amos’s unique position within the 1990s rock landscape.

Under the Pink solidified Tori Amos’s status as a major voice in alternative music, following the success of her debut Little Earthquakes. The album debuted at number one on the UK Albums Chart and reached number 12 on the US Billboard 200, driven by hit singles such as “Cornflake Girl” and “God.” It received widespread critical acclaim for its lyrical depth, musical innovation, and Amos’s powerful performances. The album’s introspective and often challenging content, combined with its commercial success, established it as a landmark release in Amos’s discography and a defining work of 1990s rock.
